claim: Synaptic-soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment receptor (SNARE) proteins couple their stage-wise folding/assembly to rapid exocytosis of neurotransmitters in a Munc18-1-dependent manner.
source: Synaptic-soluble N-ethylmaleimide-sensitive factor attachment receptor (SNARE) proteins couple their stage-wise folding/assembly to rapid exocytosis of neurotransmitters in a Munc18-1-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the abstract summarizing the main finding of the study.

claim: Using optical tweezers, four distinct stages of assembly in SNARE N-terminal, middle, C-terminal, and linker domains (NTD, MD, CTD, and LD) were observed.
source: Using optical tweezers, we observed four distinct stages of assembly in SNARE N-terminal, middle, C-terminal, and linker domains (or NTD, MD, CTD, and LD, respectively).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental observations using optical tweezers as described in the abstract and detailed in the results.

claim: SNARE layer mutations differentially affect SNARE assembly.
source: We found that SNARE layer mutations differentially affect SNARE assembly.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data on various mutations presented in the results section.

claim: NTD is responsible for vesicle docking.
source: Comparison of their effects on SNARE assembly and on exocytosis reveals that NTD and CTD are responsible for vesicle docking and fusion, respectively, whereas MD regulates SNARE assembly and fusion.
evidence: This functional assignment is based on comparison of mutation effects on SNARE assembly and exocytosis.

claim: CTD is responsible for vesicle fusion.
source: Comparison of their effects on SNARE assembly and on exocytosis reveals that NTD and CTD are responsible for vesicle docking and fusion, respectively, whereas MD regulates SNARE assembly and fusion.
evidence: This functional assignment is based on comparison of mutation effects on SNARE assembly and exocytosis.

claim: MD regulates SNARE assembly and fusion.
source: Comparison of their effects on SNARE assembly and on exocytosis reveals that NTD and CTD are responsible for vesicle docking and fusion, respectively, whereas MD regulates SNARE assembly and fusion.
evidence: This functional assignment is based on comparison of mutation effects on SNARE assembly and exocytosis.

claim: Munc18-1 initiates SNARE assembly independent of syntaxin N-terminal regulatory domain (NRD).
source: Munc18-1 initiates SNARE assembly and structures t-SNARE C-terminus independent of syntaxin N-terminal regulatory domain (NRD) and stabilizes the half-zippered SNARE complex dependent upon the NRD.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing de novo SNARE assembly with and without NRD.

claim: Munc18-1 structures t-SNARE C-terminus independent of syntaxin NRD.
source: Munc18-1 initiates SNARE assembly and structures t-SNARE C-terminus independent of syntaxin N-terminal regulatory domain (NRD) and stabilizes the half-zippered SNARE complex dependent upon the NRD.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental observations of Munc18-1 binding to SNARE complexes lacking NRD.

claim: Munc18-1 stabilizes the half-zippered SNARE complex dependent upon the NRD.
source: Munc18-1 initiates SNARE assembly and structures t-SNARE C-terminus independent of syntaxin N-terminal regulatory domain (NRD) and stabilizes the half-zippered SNARE complex dependent upon the NRD.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data showing different Munc18-1 activities with and without NRD.

claim: SNAREs are evolutionarily conserved molecular machines that drive fusion of transport vesicles with their target membranes.
source: SNAREs are evolutionarily conserved molecular machines that drive fusion of transport vesicles with their target membranes, thereby transferring materials and information between different cells or cellular compartments (Sudhof and Rothman, 2009; Wickner and Schekman, 2008; Jahn and Fasshauer, 2012).
evidence: This is a well-established fact in the field, supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SNARE-mediated membrane fusion requires cognate cytoplasmic Sec1p/Munc18 (SM) proteins.
source: In the cell, SNARE-mediated membrane fusion requires cognate cytoplasmic Sec1p/Munc18 (SM) proteins (Verhage et al., 2000).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Mutations in SNARE and SM proteins have been associated with many important human diseases.
source: Mutations in SNARE and SM proteins have been associated with many important human diseases (Sudhof, 2014; Shen et al., 2014; Saitsu et al., 2008; Shen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous literature.

claim: Fusion of synaptic vesicles with the pre-synaptic plasma membrane mediates neurotransmitter release at neuronal and neuromuscular junctions.
source: Fusion of synaptic vesicles with the pre-synaptic plasma membrane mediates neurotransmitter release at neuronal and neuromuscular junctions (Sudhof and Rothman, 2009).
evidence: This is a well-established fact supported by citation.

claim: The fusion requires the vesicle-anchored v-SNARE VAMP2, the plasma-membrane-associated t-SNAREs syntaxin-1 and SNAP-25, and the SM-protein Munc18-1.
source: The fusion requires the vesicle-anchored v-SNARE VAMP2 (also called synaptobrevin), the plasma-membrane-associated t-SNAREs syntaxin-1 and SNAP-25 (Figure 1A), and the SM-protein Munc18-1 (Sollner et al., 1993; Verhage et al., 2000; Sudhof, 2014; Rothman, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations and reference to Figure 1A showing the SNARE proteins.

claim: The t- and v-SNAREs first form a partial trans-SNARE complex bridging the two membranes with the assistance of many regulatory proteins, which docks the vesicle to the plasma membrane.
source: Extensive evidence suggests that the t- and v-SNAREs first form a partial trans-SNARE complex bridging the two membranes with the assistance of many regulatory proteins, including Munc18-1, synaptotagmin, complexin, and Munc13, which docks the vesicle to the plasma membrane (Xu et al., 1999; Melia et al., 2002; Gao et al., 2012; Sudhof, 2014; Rothman, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous work.

claim: Upon the arrival of an action potential and resultant Ca2+ influx, the trans-SNARE complex rapidly zippers to complete its assembly and membrane fusion.
source: Upon the arrival of an action potential and resultant Ca2+ influx, the trans-SNARE complex rapidly zippers to complete its assembly and membrane fusion.
evidence: This describes the mechanism of Ca2+-triggered fusion based on established knowledge.

claim: An alternative model suggests that SNARE assembly only starts after Ca2+ triggering and completes in one step without any intermediates.
source: However, an alternative model suggests that SNARE assembly only starts after Ca2+ triggering and completes in one step without any intermediates (Jahn and Fasshauer, 2012).
evidence: This is an alternative hypothesis from the literature, supported by citation.

claim: The fully assembled SNARE complex forms a stable parallel four-helix bundle.
source: The fully assembled SNARE complex forms a stable parallel four-helix bundle (Sutton et al., 1998; Stein et al., 2009) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by citations to structural studies and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The tight SNARE association is mediated by 15 layers of hydrophobic amino acids and a central ionic layer in the core of the bundle.
source: The tight SNARE association is mediated by 15 layers of hydrophobic amino acids and a central ionic layer in the core of the bundle (Fasshauer et al., 1998) (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is supported by citation and reference to Figure 1A showing the layer structure.

claim: Layer mutations differentially impact synaptic exocytosis, brain functions, and human psychology.
source: Numerous studies have shown that layer mutations differentially impact synaptic exocytosis, brain functions, and human psychology (Walter et al., 2010; Mohrmann et al., 2010; Shen et al., 2014; Sudhof, 2014).
evidence: This is supported by multiple citations to previous studies.

claim: Munc18-1 can significantly enhance the rate and specificity of SNARE-mediated membrane fusion under certain conditions.
source: On one hand, Munc18-1 can significantly enhance the rate and specificity of SNARE-mediated membrane fusion under certain conditions (Shen et al., 2007; Rathore et al., 2010; Yu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous experimental work.

claim: Munc18-1 tightly associates with syntaxin in a closed conformation that inhibits SNARE assembly.
source: On the other hand, Munc18-1 tightly associates with syntaxin in a closed conformation that inhibits SNARE assembly (Colbert et al., 2013; Burkhardt et al., 2008; Dulubova et al., 1999).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous structural and biochemical studies.

claim: Munc18-1 binds with over micromolar affinities to the t-SNARE complex, VAMP2, and the ternary SNARE complex.
source: Munc18-1 also binds with over micromolar affinities to the t-SNARE complex (Zhang et al., 2015), VAMP2 (Parisotto et al., 2014; Xu et al., 2010b), and the ternary SNARE complex (Dulubova et al., 2007; Shen et al., 2007; Rathore et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous binding studies.

claim: SNAREs couple their exergonic folding to membrane fusion.
source: SNAREs couple their exergonic folding to membrane fusion (Sudhof and Rothman, 2009; Rothman, 2014).
evidence: This is a fundamental principle of SNARE function supported by citations.

claim: A thermodynamic coupling mechanism predicts that any perturbation in SNARE assembly impacts membrane fusion.
source: Such a thermodynamic coupling mechanism predicts that any perturbation in SNARE assembly impacts membrane fusion.
evidence: This is a logical inference from the thermodynamic coupling principle.

claim: VAMP2 layer mutation F77A abolished exocytosis.
source: For example, although VAMP2 layer mutation F77A abolished exocytosis, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements showed that the mutation barely changed SNARE folding energy (Walter et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous experimental work.

claim: ITC measurements showed that F77A mutation barely changed SNARE folding energy.
source: For example, although VAMP2 layer mutation F77A abolished exocytosis, isothermal titration calorimetry (ITC) measurements showed that the mutation barely changed SNARE folding energy (Walter et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous ITC measurements.

claim: All SNARE complexes are similarly unzipped in two reversible steps and one irreversible step, corresponding to sequential disassembly of SNARE LD, CTD, and NTD at increasing forces.
source: We have found that all the SNARE complexes are similarly unzipped in two reversible steps and one irreversible step, corresponding to sequential disassembly of SNARE LD, CTD, and NTD at increasing forces.
evidence: This is based on previous single-molecule measurements by the authors.

claim: Complete stage-wise assembly has not directly been observed due to the slow NTD association.
source: However, complete stage-wise assembly has not directly been observed, due to the slow NTD association.
evidence: This identifies a limitation of previous work that the current study addresses.

claim: A new SNARE construct was developed that allowed measurement of reversible SNARE assembly and disassembly in four distinct stages.
source: Here, we developed a new SNARE construct that allowed us to measure reversible SNARE assembly and disassembly in four distinct stages and to determine their folding energies and kinetics (Figure 1B).
evidence: This describes the methodological advance of the current study, with reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The NRD contains a ~15 amino acid N-terminal peptide (N-peptide) and a C-terminal Habc domain in a three-helix bundle conformation.
source: The NRD contains a ~15 amino acid (a.a.) N-terminal peptide (N-peptide) and a C-terminal Habc domain in a three-helix bundle conformation (Fernandez et al., 1998) (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is supported by citation to structural work and reference to Figure 1B.

claim: The construct crosslinked near the -6 hydrophobic layer exhibited fast and reversible NTD folding/unfolding transition.
source: We examined six such SNARE constructs crosslinked at different sites (Figure 1—figure supplements 1,2) and found that the construct crosslinked near the -6 hydrophobic layer exhibited fast and reversible NTD folding/unfolding transition (Figure 1A,B,C).
evidence: This is based on experimental data from testing different constructs.

claim: The fast NTD folding observed implicates the existence of a nucleation site for NTD zippering near or N-terminal to the -6 layer.
source: Compared to the slow and irreversible NTD association detected for the SNARE constructs crosslinked N-terminal to the -7 layer (Gao et al., 2012) (Figure 1—figure supplements 1–2, construct I), the fast NTD folding observed here implicated the existence of a nucleation site for NTD zippering near or N-terminal to the -6 layer.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of different constructs.

claim: The FECs showed four reversible transitions with fast extension flickering and one irreversible unfolding transition, indicating cooperative unfolding/refolding of five SNARE domains.
source: The force-extension curves (FECs) obtained by pulling and then relaxing a single SNARE complex (Figure 1C) showed four reversible transitions with fast extension flickering (among states 1 to 5) and one irreversible unfolding transition (from states 5 to 6), indicating cooperative unfolding/refolding of five SNARE domains (Video 1).
evidence: This is based on direct experimental observations shown in Figure 1C and Video 1.

claim: The FECs associated with states 1–3 were identical to the FECs previously reported and independent of the N-terminal crosslinking.
source: The FECs associated with states 1–3 were identical to the FECs previously reported (Gao et al., 2012) and independent of the N-terminal crosslinking (Figure 1—figure supplement 2,3).
evidence: This is based on comparison with previous data and control experiments.

claim: States 1, 2, and 3 are the fully folded, the LD-unfolded, and the partially-zippered SNARE complexes, respectively.
source: The comparison suggests that the states 1, 2, and 3 are the fully folded, the LD-unfolded, and the partially-zippered SNARE complexes, respectively (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison with previous work and structural analysis.

claim: Relaxing the complex from state 5 led to a FEC that overlaps the FEC in the pulling phase, indicating complete and reversible reassembly of the SNARE complex.
source: Relaxing the complex from state 5 led to a FEC that overlaps the FEC in the pulling phase, indicating complete and reversible reassembly of the SNARE complex (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on experimental observation shown in the figure supplement.

claim: Pulling the complex in state 5 to higher forces saw a small rip resulting from unfolding of the remaining t-SNARE complex (from state 5 to state 6).
source: However, pulling the complex in state 5 to higher forces saw a small rip resulting from unfolding of the remaining t-SNARE complex (from state 5 to state 6) (Gao et al., 2012) (Figure 1C,D).
evidence: This is based on experimental observation and comparison with previous work.

claim: No single SNARE re-assembly event was detected among 45 different SNARE complexes tested after complete unfolding.
source: Unexpectedly, no single SNARE re-assembly event was detected among 45 different SNARE complexes tested.
evidence: This is a direct experimental observation.

claim: The failure of reassembly was caused by dissociation of the SNAP-25 molecule upon t-SNARE unfolding.
source: Consistent with our previous observation (Gao et al., 2012), the failure of reassembly was caused by dissociation of the SNAP-25 molecule upon t-SNARE unfolding, because adding 15 µM SNAP-25 into the solution rescued the assembly (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is based on experimental observation and rescue experiment.

claim: An additional state (state 4) was hidden in the NTD transition with a maximum lifetime of ~1 ms.
source: Close inspection shows an additional state hidden in the NTD transition, state 4 (Figure 1—figure supplement 5). This state had a maximum lifetime of ~1 ms and rapidly transited between state 3 and state 5 (Figure 2A and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on detailed analysis of high-bandwidth data.

claim: In the partially-zippered state 3, the VAMP2 CTD and the t-SNARE CTD are unfolded from layer +8 to layer +3 and layer +5, respectively.
source: In the partially-zippered state 3, the VAMP2 CTD and the t-SNARE CTD are unfolded from layer +8 to layer +3 and layer +5, respectively, whereas the remainder of the SNAREs are largely helical as in the four-helix bundle.
evidence: This structural assignment is based on analysis of extension changes.

claim: This structure is consistent with that of a different trans-SNARE complex located on the yeast vacuole.
source: This structure is consistent with that of a different trans-SNARE complex located on the yeast vacuole (Schwartz and Merz, 2009).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous structural work on a different SNARE complex.

claim: In the MD-unfolded state 4, VAMP2 is unfolded further to the ionic layer.
source: In the MD-unfolded state 4, VAMP2 is unfolded further to the ionic layer.
evidence: This structural assignment is based on analysis of extension changes.

claim: The MD consists of the ionic layer (0 layer) and the +1 and +2 layers exclusively comprising leucine and isoleucine residues known to form strong coiled coils.
source: Therefore, the MD consists of the ionic layer (0 layer) and the +1 and +2 layers exclusively comprising leucine and isoleucine residues known to form strong coiled coils (Figure 1A), which leads to the higher mechanical stability of the MD than the CTD and their distinct transitions.
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and known properties of leucine/isoleucine coiled coils.

claim: In the unzipped SNARE state 5, the t-SNARE complex remains in a three-helix bundle conformation, but with a frayed C-terminus (Tc).
source: In the unzipped SNARE state 5, the t-SNARE complex remains in a three-helix bundle conformation, but with a frayed C-terminus (Tc).
evidence: This structural assignment is based on analysis of extension changes and confirmed by Vc peptide binding experiments.

claim: The folding energies of NTD, MD, and CTD are 25 (±2, S.D.) kBT, 13 (±1) kBT, and 22 (±3) kBT, respectively.
source: Specifically, the folding energies of NTD, MD, and CTD are 25 (±2, S.D.) kBT, 13 (±1) kBT, and 22 (±3) kBT, respectively, where kB is the Boltzmann constant and T= 296 K the room temperature, with kBT=0.59 kcal/mol.
evidence: These values are derived from fitting experimental data to a thermodynamic model.

claim: The SNARE complex has total zippering energy of 68 (±4) kBT, including 8 (±2) kBT LD folding energy.
source: Thus, the SNARE complex has total zippering energy of 68 (±4) kBT, including 8 (±2) kBT LD folding energy (Gao et al., 2012).
evidence: This is calculated from the sum of individual domain energies.

claim: Folding of the NTD and CTD is downhill.
source: Folding of the NTD and CTD is downhill.
evidence: This is inferred from the energy landscape analysis.

claim: The MD has a folding energy barrier of 5.0 (±0.6) kBT located close to the ionic layer.
source: In contrast, the MD has a folding energy barrier of 5.0 (±0.6) kBT located close to the ionic layer, indicating a high-energy penalty to dehydrate the ionic layer for MD assembly (Rebane, et al., 2016).
evidence: This is derived from kinetic analysis and modeling.

claim: Binding of the Vc peptide to the t-SNARE complex induces a coil-to-helix transition in Tc.
source: We predicted that binding of the Vc peptide to the t-SNARE complex would induce a coil-to-helix transition in Tc and inhibit or attenuate SNARE zippering into the two partially-zippered states 3 and 4.
evidence: This prediction is confirmed by experimental observations of extension changes upon Vc binding.

claim: The Vc peptide frequently bound to the SNARE complex in the presence of 44 μM Vc peptide in the solution.
source: In the presence of 44 μM Vc peptide in the solution, we found that the Vc peptide frequently bound to the SNARE complex.
evidence: This is a direct experimental observation.

claim: Once bound, the Vc peptide did not dissociate from the SNARE complex, indicating that the Vc peptide outcompeted the VAMP2 molecule to tightly associate with the t-SNARE complex.
source: Once bound, the Vc peptide did not dissociate from the SNARE complex, indicating that the Vc peptide outcompeted the VAMP2 molecule to tightly associate with the t-SNARE complex under our experimental conditions.
evidence: This is based on experimental observation of long-lived Vc-bound states.

claim: The Vc-bound states have a unimodal extension distribution whose peak extension is 2.7 nm less than the average extension of the NTD-unfolded state 5.
source: The Vc-bound SNARE states have a unimodal extension distribution (Figure 3C), whose peak extension is 2.7 nm less than the average extension of the NTD-unfolded state 5, with an average shortening of 2.3 (±0.5, N=8) nm (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is based on analysis of extension distributions shown in Figure 3.

claim: The extension shortening upon Vc binding is consistent with the predicted coil-to-helix transition in Tc, confirming the disordered Tc.
source: The extension shortening upon Vc binding is consistent with the predicted coil-to-helix transition in Tc, confirming the disordered Tc.
evidence: This is an inference based on comparison of predicted and observed extension changes.

claim: The Vc peptide predominantly stabilized the SNARE complex in the Vn-unfolded state (state 8).
source: The comparison of the extension distributions also reveals that the Vc peptide predominantly stabilized the SNARE complex in the Vn-unfolded state (state 8) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of extension distributions.

claim: The Vc peptide acted as a roadblock to attenuate VAMP2 from zippering.
source: Thus, upon binding to the t-SNARE complex, the Vc peptide acted as a roadblock to attenuate VAMP2 from zippering.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that partially zippered states were only transient.

claim: The Vc peptide was displaced by the VAMP2 molecule at an average force of 6 (± 1) pN upon relaxation.
source: However, the Vc peptide was displaced by the VAMP2 molecule at an average force of 6 (± 1) pN upon relaxation.
evidence: This is a direct experimental observation.

claim: Most SNARE complexes containing single alanine substitutions in the NTD, except for M46A, exhibit similar FECs and transition kinetics as the wild-type.
source: All SNARE complexes containing single alanine substitutions in the NTD, except for M46A, exhibit similar FECs and transition kinetics as the wild-type (Figures 4–6 and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements of multiple mutants.

claim: Single alanine substitutions in the NTD generally have minor impact on SNARE assembly.
source: Therefore, single alanine substitutions in the NTD generally have minor impact on SNARE assembly.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that most NTD mutations have similar properties to wild-type.

claim: M46A reduced the stability of NTD, as indicated by a small decrease in the force for NTD transition compared to the wild-type.
source: In contrast, M46A reduced the stability of NTD, as is indicated by a small decrease in the force for NTD transition compared to the wild-type (Figures 4 and 6).
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements shown in the figures.

claim: M46A altered SNARE assembly kinetics and pathway by causing MD and NTD to transit cooperatively as one unit.
source: The approximately equal mechanical stabilities of MD and NTD now led to disappearance of the intermediate state 4 (Figure 5). Consequently, both MD and NTD transited cooperatively as one unit (designated as MD_NTD) between the CTD-unfolded state 3 and the unzipped state 5 (Figure 4—figure supplement 1), in contrast with the sequential MD and NTD transitions (designated as MD+NTD) seen for the wild-type SNARE complex (Figure 2A). Thus, M46A altered SNARE assembly kinetics and pathway.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations and analysis of transition pathways.

claim: The double mutation V39A/V42A dramatically decreased the folding rate of NTD.
source: Finally, the double mutation V39A/V42A dramatically decreased the folding rate of NTD (Figure 5).
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements shown in Figure 5.

claim: V39A/V42A destabilized NTD by 3 kBT.
source: In addition, it destabilized NTD by 3 kBT (Figure 7).
evidence: This is based on energy measurements shown in Figure 7.

claim: R56A destabilized both NTD and CTD, indicating that the ionic layer globally stabilizes the SNARE complex.
source: First, R56A destabilized both NTD and CTD (Figures 4 and 7), indicating that the ionic layer globally stabilizes the SNARE complex (Rebane, et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements and inference about the role of the ionic layer.

claim: R56A increased the extension change associated with the MD transition, corroborating the independent MD transition and the N-terminal border position of R56 in the MD.
source: In addition, R56A increased the extension change associated with the MD transition (Figure 5 and Figure 5—figure supplement 2), corroborating the independent MD transition and the N-terminal border position of R56 in the MD.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations supporting the structural model.

claim: L60A (+1) and L63A (+2) abolished the independent MD transition and caused MD to merge with CTD.
source: In contrast, L60A (+1) and L63A (+2) abolished the independent MD transition and caused MD to merge with CTD (Figure 5).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 5.

claim: Mutations at +1 and +2 layers altered the pathway of SNARE assembly, in which the distinct MD assembly was bypassed.
source: Therefore, mutations at +1 and +2 layers altered the pathway of SNARE assembly, in which the distinct MD assembly was bypassed.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that MD and CTD fold cooperatively in these mutants.

claim: All MD mutations abolished the energy barrier in MD folding.
source: Accordingly, all MD mutations abolished the energy barrier in MD folding (Rebane, et al., 2016) (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is based on analysis of energy landscapes for mutants.

claim: All MD mutants frequently and abruptly switched their transition kinetics, indicating an important role of MD in accurate and robust SNARE assembly.
source: Finally, we found that all MD mutants frequently and abruptly switched their transition kinetics (Figure 8), indicating an important role of MD in accurate and robust SNARE assembly.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations of kinetic heterogeneity shown in Figure 8.

claim: The two mutations A67S (+3) and L84A (+8) at the borders of the CTD had only minor effects on SNARE assembly.
source: The two mutations A67S (+3) and L84A (+8) at the borders of the CTD had only minor effects on SNARE assembly (Figures 4, 7, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements.

claim: L70A (+4) and F77A (+6) in VAMP2 and M71A/I192A (+5) in SNAP-25 greatly reduced the force ranges of the CTD transition.
source: In contrast, L70A (+4) and F77A (+6) in VAMP2 and M71A/I192A (+5) in SNAP-25 greatly reduced the force ranges of the CTD transition that now overlapped the LD transition.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: The +6 layer mutation weakened both CTD and LD.
source: In particular, the +6 layer mutation weakened both CTD and LD (Figures 4,6,7, and Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements.

claim: Alanine substitutions at +4, +5 and +6 layers dramatically decreased CTD folding energies by 10 kBT, 13 kBT, and 12 kBT, respectively, compared to the wild-type.
source: Correspondingly, alanine substitutions at +4, +5 and +6 layers dramatically decreased CTD folding energies by 10 kBT, 13 kBT, and 12 kBT, respectively, compared to the wild-type.
evidence: This is based on energy measurements.

claim: The energy measurement of F77A contrasts with the previous measurement by ITC and is consistent with its ablation of exocytosis.
source: Our energy measurement of F77A contrasts with the previous measurement by ITC and is consistent with its ablation of exocytosis (Walter et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous work showing the current measurements resolve a discrepancy.

claim: The syntaxin mutation T251I (+7) increased the CTD zippering energy by 5 kBT.
source: The syntaxin mutation T251I (+7) is unusual, because it increased the CTD zippering energy by 5 kBT (Figures 4 and 7), quantitatively confirming the previous inference based on structural modeling (Lagow et al., 2007).
evidence: This is based on energy measurements confirming a previous prediction.

claim: The CTD stability is sensitive to mutations in layers from +4 to +7.
source: Taken together, the CTD stability is sensitive to mutations in layers from +4 to +7.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the pattern of mutation effects.

claim: In the presence of 10 µM Munc18-1, 45% of 113 completely unfolded SNARE complexes showed full reassembly.
source: In contrast, in the presence of 10 µM Munc18-1, 45% of 113 completely unfolded SNARE complexes showed full reassembly (Figure 9A,B).
evidence: This is a direct experimental observation.

claim: Munc18-1 held the SNAP-25 molecule together with the tethered syntaxin or VAMP2 as t-SNARE unfolded, facilitating de novo SNARE assembly.
source: This observation suggests that Munc18-1 held the SNAP-25 molecule together with the tethered syntaxin or VAMP2 as t-SNARE unfolded, facilitating de novo SNARE assembly.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that Munc18-1 enables reassembly that doesn't occur without it.

claim: The SNARE assembly occurred in a force range of 1-16 pN, with an average force of 8.5 pN.
source: The SNARE assembly occurred in a force range of 1-16 pN, with an average force of 8.5 pN (Figure 9C).
evidence: This is based on analysis of force distributions shown in Figure 9C.

claim: The probability to observe a SNARE reassembly event was 0.45 under experimental conditions, but the probability to detect a SNARE reassembly event after another was 0.8.
source: Although the probability to observe a SNARE reassembly event was 0.45 under our experimental conditions, the probability to detect a SNARE reassembly event after another was 0.8, suggesting a strong correlation between the different reassembly events mediated by Munc18-1.
evidence: This is based on statistical analysis of reassembly events.

claim: The same Munc18-1 molecule mediated the consecutive reassembly events without dissociation from the SNARE complex during its multiple rounds of disassembly and reassembly.
source: An appealing interpretation for the correlation is that the same Munc18-1 molecule mediated the consecutive reassembly events without dissociation from the SNARE complex during its multiple rounds of disassembly and reassembly.
evidence: This is a proposed interpretation of the observed correlation.

claim: The Munc18-1-mediated SNARE assembly was not abolished by the two VAMP2 layer mutations L60A and L63A.
source: The Munc18-1-mediated SNARE assembly was not abolished by the two VAMP2 layer mutations L60A and L63A (Figure 9B).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations with mutants.

claim: Despite their effect on the accuracy of intrinsic SNARE assembly, neither MD mutation significantly affects Munc18-1-dependent de novo SNARE assembly.
source: This finding suggests that, despite their effect on the accuracy of intrinsic SNARE assembly, neither MD mutation significantly affect Munc18-1-dependent de novo SNARE assembly.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that MD mutants still show Munc18-1-mediated assembly.

claim: Munc18-1 may mediate de novo SNARE assembly via a t-SNARE intermediate.
source: Thus, Munc18-1 may mediate de novo SNARE assembly via a t-SNARE intermediate.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of two-step assembly with construct I.

claim: A series of prominent long-dwelling states were observed in the middle of fast SNARE transitions under constant forces, revealing a new Munc18-1-dependent state.
source: Under constant forces, we observed a series of prominent long-dwelling states in the middle of fast SNARE transitions (Figure 10A,B), revealing a new Munc18-1-dependent state.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations shown in Figure 10.

claim: The Munc18-1-stabilized state lasted from 0.03 to ~30 s, with an average dwell time of 2.8 s.
source: The state lasted from 0.03 to ~30 s, with an average dwell time of 2.8 s (Figure 10C) and was detected in a force range of 15-19 pN, with an average of 17.1 pN (Figure 10D).
evidence: This is based on analysis of dwell times and forces shown in Figure 10.

claim: The new state has an extension corresponding to VAMP2 unzipped to a position between layers 0 and +1, and is thus a half-zippered state (state 9).
source: The new state has an extension corresponding to VAMP2 unzipped to a position between layers 0 and +1 (Figure 10E), and is thus a half-zippered state (state 9).
evidence: This structural assignment is based on analysis of extension.

claim: L70A did not significantly affect the Munc18-1-stabilized half-zippered state, implying that Munc18-1 did not strongly interact with L70 in this observed Munc18-1 activity.
source: We found that L70A did not significantly affect the Munc18-1-stabilized half-zippered state (Figure 10A, iii), implying that Munc18-1 did not strongly interact with L70 in this observed Munc18-1 activity.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that the mutation doesn't affect this Munc18-1 activity.

claim: Munc18-1 might partly bind the C-terminal domain of the t-SNARE in the SNARE complex to attenuate CTD zippering.
source: Instead, Munc18-1 might partly bind the C-terminal domain of the t-SNARE in the SNARE complex to attenuate CTD zippering.
evidence: This is a proposed mechanism based on the observation that Munc18-1 stabilizes a half-zippered state.

claim: Munc18-1 stabilized the half-zippered SNARE complex in a force-dependent manner.
source: In conclusion, Munc18-1 stabilized the half-zippered SNARE complex in a force-dependent manner.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the observation that the half-zippered state only appears in a specific force range.

claim: The trans-SNARE complex is likely half-zippered.
source: Because the trans-SNARE complex is likely half-zippered (Gao et al., 2012; Kyoung et al., 2011; Min et al., 2013; Li et al., 2014), our observation corroborates that Munc18-1 enhances assembly of trans-SNARE complexes to promote membrane fusion (Shen et al., 2007; Rathore et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous work and the current observations.

claim: Munc18-1 requires the NRD to enhance membrane fusion in vitro and exocytosis in vivo.
source: Previous experiments show that Munc18-1 requires the NRD to enhance membrane fusion in vitro and exocytosis in vivo (Shen et al., 2007; Dulubova et al., 2007; Zhou et al., 2013).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous experimental work.

claim: Munc18-1 is recruited by the N-peptide in the NRD to bind trans-SNARE complexes.
source: Specifically, Munc18-1 is recruited by the N-peptide in the NRD to bind trans-SNARE complexes (Shen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on citation to previous work.

claim: Once Munc18-1 associates with trans-SNARE complexes, the NRD becomes dispensable for subsequent membrane fusion.
source: Interestingly, once Munc18-1 associates with trans-SNARE complexes, the NRD becomes dispensable for subsequent membrane fusion (Rathore et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on citation to previous work.

claim: Munc18-1 binds SNARE complexes in both NRD-dependent and NRD-independent modes and can dynamically transit between the two binding modes.
source: These findings suggest that Munc18-1 binds SNARE complexes in both NRD-dependent and NRD-independent modes and can dynamically transit between the two binding modes (Hu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference based on previous findings cited.

claim: The NRD removal did not cause significant changes in the intrinsic stage-wise SNARE assembly.
source: The NRD removal did not cause significant changes in the intrinsic stage-wise SNARE assembly (Figure 1C,2A, -NRD), which suggests that the NRD barely interacted with the SNARE motifs.
evidence: This is based on comparison of FECs with and without NRD.

claim: The NRD removal did not alter the de novo SNARE assembly, indicating that the NRD is dispensable for this Munc18-1-dependent activity.
source: Furthermore, the NRD removal did not alter the de novo SNARE assembly (marked by red arrows in Figure 11A, #1, and 9B), indicating that the NRD is dispensable for this Munc18-1-dependent activity.
evidence: This is based on experimental observations with NRD-deleted constructs.

claim: Munc18-1 no longer stabilized the half-zippered state well after NRD removal.
source: However, Munc18-1 no longer stabilized the half-zippered state well (Figure 11B,C and Figure 11-figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations with NRD-deleted constructs.

claim: Munc18-1 mainly stabilized a novel state (state 11) with a distinct extension that was 1–3.5 nm less than the NTD-unfolded state 5 after NRD removal.
source: Instead, Munc18-1 mainly stabilized a novel state (state 11) with a distinct extension that was 1–3.5 nm less than the NTD-unfolded state 5 (Figure 11D and Figure 11-figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations shown in the figures.

claim: The average extension difference between state 11 and state 5 is 2.5 (±0.7, N=16) nm, approximately equal to the extension shortening caused by binding of the Vc peptide.
source: The average extension difference between state 11 and state 5 is 2.5 (±0.7, N=16) nm, approximately equal to the extension shortening caused by binding of the Vc peptide (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is based on comparison of extension changes.

claim: The NRD removal significantly enhances the thermodynamic stability of Munc18-1 binding to the SNARE complex.
source: Therefore, the NRD removal significantly enhances the thermodynamic stability of Munc18-1 binding to the SNARE complex.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Munc18-1-bound states last much longer without NRD.

claim: In the absence of NRD, Munc18-1 tightly bound t-SNARE and structured Tc.
source: We inferred that state 11 has a conformation similar to the NTD-unfolded state 5, except that Munc18-1 is associated with a structured Tc in a way similar to the Vc peptide (Figure 11E). Indeed, upon SNARE binding Munc18-1 induced approximately equal extension shortening (2.5 ± 0.7 nm) from state 5 as the Vc peptide (2.3 ± 0.5 nm) did. Therefore, in the absence of NRD, Munc18-1 tightly bound t-SNARE and structured Tc.
evidence: This is inferred from comparison of extension changes with Vc peptide.

claim: Munc18-1 must also bind amino acids in t-SNARE N-terminal to −1 layer to interfere with NTD zippering.
source: Because SNARE zippering was attenuated, Munc18-1 must also bind amino acids in t-SNARE N-terminal to −1 layer to interfere with NTD zippering (Figure 11E).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that NTD zippering is attenuated.

claim: In state 10, VAMP2 was zippered to a position between −2 and −1 layers.
source: Accordingly, we estimated that in state 10 VAMP2 was zippered to a position between −2 and −1 layers, in contrast with the half-zippered state 9 (between 0 and +1 layers).
evidence: This is estimated based on extension analysis and comparison with state 9.

claim: Munc18-1 and the Vc peptide probably promote membrane fusion by the same mechanism: They structure Tc, stabilize the t-SNARE complex, and inhibit SNARE mis-assembly.
source: These observations suggest that Munc18-1 and the Vc peptide probably promote membrane fusion by the same mechanism: They structure Tc, stabilize the t-SNARE complex, and inhibit SNARE mis-assembly (Pobbati et al., 2006), which outcompete their adverse effects of attenuating SNARE zippering.
evidence: This is inferred from the similar effects of Munc18-1 and Vc peptide on SNARE structure.

claim: Munc18-1 occasionally bypassed the NRD to similarly attenuate zippering and structure Tc of the SNARE complex containing the NRD.
source: Finally, we found that Munc18-1 occasionally (4 out of 113) bypassed the NRD to similarly attenuate zippering and structure Tc of the SNARE complex containing the NRD (Figure 11- figure supplement 2,3).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations.

claim: Munc18-1 may transit between the NRD-dependent and the NRD-independent SNARE-binding modes.
source: This finding suggests that Munc18-1 may transit between the NRD-dependent and the NRD-independent SNARE-binding modes, consistent with previous observations (Rathore et al., 2010; Hu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that both modes can occur and is consistent with previous work.

claim: Munc18-1 interacts with the SNARE bundle in at least two modes and differentially regulates SNARE zippering.
source: In conclusion, we observed that Munc18-1 interacts with the SNARE bundle in at least two modes and differentially regulates SNARE zippering: In an NRD-dependent mode, Munc18-1 stabilizes the half-zippered state, while in an NRD-independent mode, Munc18-1 structures Tc.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the experimental observations.

claim: Partial refolding of the completely unfolded SNARE complex was sometimes observed upon relaxation in the presence of Munc18-1.
source: Upon relaxation of the completely unfolded SNARE complex in the presence of Munc18-1, partial refolding of the complex was sometimes observed (17 out of 113 SNARE complexes tested) (Figure 12A).
evidence: This is a direct experimental observation.

claim: The refolding process was reversible and fast in the force range of 4-8 pN, with an average equilibrium force of 6.1 (±0.8) pN and an extension change of ~4 nm.
source: The refolding process was reversible and fast in the force range of 4-8 pN, with an average equilibrium force of 6.1 (±0.8) pN and an extension change of ~4 nm (Figure 12B).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the transition shown in Figure 12B.

claim: The transition required both Munc18-1 and the NRD, because the transition disappeared when either Munc18-1 was omitted or the NRD was removed.
source: This transition required both Munc18-1 and the NRD, because the transition disappeared when either Munc18-1 was omitted or the NRD was removed.
evidence: This is based on control experiments.

claim: The transition resulted from the Munc18-1-mediated transition of the syntaxin molecule between the closed conformation and the open conformation.
source: We concluded that the transition resulted from the Munc18-1-mediated transition of the syntaxin molecule between the closed conformation and the open conformation (Figure 12C) (Dulubova et al., 1999).
evidence: This is inferred from the properties of the transition and comparison with known syntaxin conformations.

claim: A lower limit of ~−7 kBT was estimated for the free energy of the closed state relative to the open state.
source: Consequently, we estimated a lower limit of ~−7 kBT for the free energy of the closed state relative to the open state, based on the measured mechanical work required to unfold the closed state.
evidence: This is calculated from the measured force and extension change.

claim: The relatively small energy difference revealed that the closed syntaxin could spontaneously open to participate in SNARE assembly.
source: The relatively small energy difference revealed that the closed syntaxin could spontaneously open to participate in SNARE assembly.
evidence: This is an inference based on the measured energy difference.

claim: The measurement is consistent with a recent observation that syntaxin can spontaneously open.
source: However, our measurement is consistent with a recent observation that syntaxin can spontaneously open (Hu et al., 2011; Pertsinidis et al., 2013).
evidence: This is a comparison with previous work.

claim: Munc18-1 must remain attached to the syntaxin molecule during the whole syntaxin transition process.
source: Given the overall low frequency to observe the syntaxin transition under our experimental conditions (<0.01 s-1), Munc18-1 must remain attached to the syntaxin molecule during the whole syntaxin transition process (Figure 12B), suggesting a multivalent interaction between Munc18-1 and syntaxin (Colbert et al., 2013; Hu et al., 2011; Burkhardt et al., 2008).
evidence: This is inferred from the low frequency of the transition.

claim: Munc18-1 binding and syntaxin closing do not necessarily coincide: syntaxin could stay in an open state while Munc18-1 remained attached to part of the syntaxin molecule.
source: This finding shows that Munc18-1 binding and syntaxin closing do not necessarily coincide: syntaxin could stay in an open state while Munc18-1 remained attached to part of the syntaxin molecule, including the NRD (Figure 12C) (Hu et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation of syntaxin opening/closing while Munc18-1 remains bound.

claim: The multivalent interaction reconciles the marginal stability of the closed syntaxin observed and the overall high affinity between Munc18-1 and syntaxin.
source: The multivalent interaction also reconciles the marginal stability of the closed syntaxin observed by us and the overall high affinity between Munc18-1 and syntaxin.
evidence: This is an inference explaining how the observations are consistent.

claim: Syntaxin alone unfolded in a force range of 15-25 pN and refolded at 3-7 pN, due to irreversible unfolding and refolding of the Habc domain.
source: Syntaxin alone unfolded in a force range of 15-25 pN and refolded at 3-7 pN, due to irreversible unfolding and refolding of the Habc domain (Figure 13C).
evidence: This is based on experimental measurements of isolated syntaxin.

claim: In the presence of 10 µM Munc18-1, another transition was found in the force range of 3-8 pN that only occurred in the presence of the folded Habc, which represents the Munc18-1-mediated syntaxin opening and closing transition.
source: In the presence of 10 µM Munc18-1 in the solution, we found another transition in the force range of 3-8 pN that only occurred in the presence of the folded Habc, which represents the Munc18-1-mediated syntaxin opening and closing transition (Figure 13B).
evidence: This is based on experimental observations with isolated syntaxin in the presence of Munc18-1.

claim: The syntaxin transition took place in a similar low-force range with a similar extension change as observed in the previous SNARE construct, confirming the marginal stability of the closed syntaxin state.
source: Thus, the syntaxin transition took place in a similar low-force range with a similar extension change as observed in the previous SNARE construct (Figure 12C), confirming the marginal stability of the closed syntaxin state.
evidence: This is based on comparison of results from two different constructs.

claim: The presence of NRD did not significantly reduce the probability for Munc18-1 to mediate de novo SNARE assembly.
source: As a result, the presence of NRD did not significantly reduce the probability for Munc18-1 to mediate de novo SNARE assembly (Figure 9B), although the unfolded SNARE motif in syntaxin could alternatively enter the closed state (Figure 12C).
evidence: This is based on comparison of reassembly probabilities with and without NRD.

claim: SNARE assembly exhibited different sensitivity to mutations that correlates with their various phenotypes in vivo.
source: We found that SNARE assembly exhibited different sensitivity to mutations that correlates with their various phenotypes in vivo.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on comparison of mutation effects on assembly and exocytosis.

claim: The NTD mutation V39A/V42A reduces the number of docked vesicles, but does not change the Ca2+-triggered fusion rate of the vesicles in the readily releasable pool in chromaffin cells.
source: Compared to the wild-type SNARE complex, the NTD mutation V39A/V42A reduces the number of docked vesicles, but does not change the Ca2+-triggered fusion rate of the vesicles in the readily releasable pool in chromaffin cells, as was derived from electrophysiological measurements (Walter et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on citation to previous electrophysiological studies.

claim: The same mutation destabilized NTD by 3 kBT with no change in CTD zippering energy.
source: In parallel, our measurements showed that the same mutation destabilized NTD by 3 kBT with no change in CTD zippering energy (Figure 7).
evidence: This is based on the current energy measurements.

claim: The comparison suggests that NTD association is responsible for docking, but not vesicle fusion and that the NTD folding energy dictates the number of docked vesicles.
source: The comparison suggests that NTD association is responsible for docking, but not vesicle fusion and that the NTD folding energy dictates the number of docked vesicles.
evidence: This is an inference based on correlation between NTD energy and docking phenotype.

claim: The NTD association and dissociation reaches dynamic equilibrium, consistent with dynamic vesicle docking and undocking observed in vivo and in vitro.
source: Accordingly, the NTD association and dissociation reaches dynamic equilibrium, consistent with dynamic vesicle docking and undocking observed in vivo and in vitro (Zenisek et al., 2000; Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is an inference consistent with previous observations cited.

claim: The reduced NTD association rate of the mutant should decrease the fusion rate of the vesicles in the sustained releasable pool (SRP).
source: Thus, we predicted that the reduced NTD association rate of the mutant observed by us (Figure 5A) should decrease the fusion rate of the vesicles in the sustained releasable pool (SRP).
evidence: This is a prediction based on the measured kinetic effect.

claim: The SRP fusion rate of the mutant is reduced by ~50%, confirming the prediction.
source: Indeed, the SRP fusion rate of the mutant is reduced by ~50% (Walter et al., 2010), confirming the prediction.
evidence: This is based on citation to previous work that confirms the prediction.

claim: NTD association energy and kinetics contribute to the magnitude and rate of vesicle docking, respectively.
source: Therefore, NTD association energy and kinetics contribute to the magnitude and rate of vesicle docking, respectively.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the correlation between NTD properties and docking phenotypes.

claim: Mutations that decreased CTD zippering energy by ~10 kBT, including L70A (+4) and F77A (+6) in VAMP2 and M71A/I192A (+5) in SNAP-25B, dramatically reduce the rate of exocytosis.
source: Mutations that decreased CTD zippering energy by ~10 kBT, including L70A (+4) and F77A (+6) in VAMP2 and M71A/I192A (+5) in SNAP-25B, also dramatically reduce the rate of exocytosis (Walter et al., 2010; Mohrmann et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on the current energy measurements and citations to previous exocytosis studies.

claim: I67N (+4) in SNAP-25B is a dominant mutation identified from a patient with myasthenia, ataxia, and intellectual disability.
source: Interestingly, I67N (+4) in SNAP-25B is a dominant mutation identified from a patient with myasthenia, ataxia, and intellectual disability (Shen et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on citation to a clinical study.

claim: The I67N mutation impaired neuromuscular transmission.
source: It is found that this mutation impaired neuromuscular transmission.
evidence: This is based on citation to previous work.

claim: The layers +4, +5, and +6 are crucial for CTD zippering and membrane fusion.
source: These results demonstrated that the layers +4, +5, and +6 are crucial for CTD zippering and membrane fusion.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the effects of mutations at these positions.

claim: Syntaxin T251I (+7) enhanced CTD zippering and is found to increase both spontaneous and evoked exocytosis.
source: In contrast, syntaxin T251I (+7) in syntaxin enhanced CTD zippering and is found to increase both spontaneous and evoked exocytosis (Lagow et al., 2007).
evidence: This is based on the current energy measurements and citation to previous exocytosis studies.

claim: Flies carrying the T251I mutation become paralyzed at 38°C.
source: However, flies carrying this mutation become paralyzed at 38°C.
evidence: This is based on citation to previous work.

claim: These findings are consistent with the existence of a metastable partially zippered SNARE complex in the docked state.
source: These findings are consistent with the existence of a metastable partially zippered SNARE complex in the docked state (Gao et al., 2012; Kyoung et al., 2011; Lou et al., 2015; Shin et al., 2014) and mutations that stabilize CTD destabilize the half-zippered SNARE complex, leading to mis-regulated exocytosis and reduced precision of neurotransmission.
evidence: This is an inference based on the effects of mutations and citations to previous work.

claim: The stabilities of different SNARE domains appear to be optimized to balance the accuracy and speed of membrane fusion.
source: Thus, the stabilities of different SNARE domains appear to be optimized to balance the accuracy and speed of membrane fusion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that both increasing and decreasing CTD stability can be detrimental.

claim: Other CTD mutations, A67S (+3) and L84A (+8), do not significantly change the CTD folding energy and rate, nor exocytosis.
source: Finally, other CTD mutations, A67S (+3) and L84A (+8), do not significantly change the CTD folding energy and rate, nor exocytosis (Walter et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on the current measurements and citation to previous exocytosis studies.

claim: CTD zippering directly drives membrane fusion by tightly coupling its folding energy to lowering the energy barrier of membrane fusion, thereby increasing the fusion rate.
source: In conclusion, CTD zippering directly drives membrane fusion by tightly coupling its folding energy to lowering the energy barrier of membrane fusion, thereby increasing the fusion rate.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the correlation between CTD energy and fusion rate.

claim: R56A reduced SNARE zippering energy and was found to impair membrane fusion in some reports.
source: R56A reduced SNARE zippering energy (Figure 7) and was found to impair membrane fusion in some reports (Ossig et al., 2000).
evidence: This is based on the current energy measurements and citation to previous work.

claim: L60A (+1) and L63A (+2) abolished both spontaneous and evoked exocytosis.
source: They found that the two mutations abolished both spontaneous and evoked exocytosis, implying an important role of independent MD assembly in exocytosis.
evidence: This is based on citation to previous work.

claim: An obligate pathway of SNARE assembly may be required for membrane fusion.
source: The comparison suggests that an obligate pathway of SNARE assembly may be required for membrane fusion.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observation that mutations that change the assembly pathway abolish fusion.

claim: Tight thermodynamic coupling requires specific SNARE assembly intermediates and pathways.
source: We showed that tight thermodynamic coupling requires specific SNARE assembly intermediates and pathways.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that pathway-altering mutations abolish fusion.

claim: The SNARE engine consists of four stages of zippering in NTD, MD, CTD, and LD with distinct functions.
source: Thus, the SNARE engine consists of four stages of zippering in NTD, MD, CTD, and LD with distinct functions.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the functional assignments.

claim: The MD serves as a checkpoint to further ensure proper SNARE assembly and as a master switch to control CTD assembly.
source: The MD serves as a checkpoint to further ensure proper SNARE assembly and as a master switch to control CTD assembly.
evidence: This is an inference based on the effects of MD mutations on assembly pathway and accuracy.

claim: The CTD acts as a power stroke that directly drives membrane fusion.
source: The CTD acts as a power stroke that directly drives membrane fusion.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the correlation between CTD energy and fusion rate.

claim: Continued zippering to LD and the transmembrane domains may provide additional energy for membrane fusion or alter the interactions between SNAREs and membranes to facilitate fusion.
source: Continued zippering to LD and the transmembrane domains may provide additional energy for membrane fusion (Stein et al., 2009) or alter the interactions between SNAREs and membranes to facilitate fusion (Ngatchou et al., 2010; Liang et al., 2013; Honigmann et al., 2013).
evidence: This is speculation based on citations to previous work.

claim: Munc18-1 regulates every stage of SNARE assembly.
source: We found that Munc18-1 regulates every stage of SNARE assembly.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the multiple Munc18-1 activities observed.

claim: Munc18-1 efficiently initiates SNARE assembly (from state ii to state v).
source: Second, we observed that Munc18-1 efficiently initiates SNARE assembly (from state ii to state v).
evidence: This is based on the observation of de novo SNARE assembly mediated by Munc18-1.

claim: Because this activity is NRD-independent, Munc18-1 likely directly binds SNARE motifs to promote SNARE assembly.
source: Because this activity is NRD-independent, Munc18-1 likely directly binds SNARE motifs to promote SNARE assembly (states ii and iii) (Shi et al., 2011).
evidence: This is an inference based on the NRD-independence of this activity.

claim: Munc18-1 did not stabilize the fully assembly SNARE complex in single-molecule experiments.
source: Finally, we did not find evidence that Munc18-1 stabilized the fully assembly SNARE complex in our single-molecule experiments, consistent with a recent report (Zhang et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on the absence of observations of Munc18-1 binding to fully assembled SNARE and citation to consistent work.

claim: Munc18-1 mainly enhances membrane fusion by catalyzing SNARE assembly, rather than by stabilizing the fully assembled SNARE complex.
source: Thus, we conclude that Munc18-1 mainly enhances membrane fusion by catalyzing SNARE assembly, rather than by stabilizing the fully assembled SNARE complex.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the observation that Munc18-1 acts on intermediates but not the final state.

claim: The rate of membrane fusion poorly correlates with the binding affinity between SM proteins and the fully assembled SNARE complexes.
source: Consistent with this view, the rate of membrane fusion poorly correlate with the binding affinity between SM proteins and the fully assembled SNARE complexes (Shen et al., 2007; Shen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous work.

claim: SNARE mutations that compromise interactions between the fully assembled SNARE complexes and their cognate SM proteins can support membrane fusion.
source: In particular, SNARE mutations that compromise interactions between the fully assembled SNARE complexes and their cognate SM proteins can support membrane fusion (Peng and Gallwitz, 2004).
evidence: This is based on citation to previous work.

claim: Munc18-1 mainly acts on the folding intermediates of SNAREs to chaperone their assembly.
source: Taking together, we conclude that Munc18-1 mainly acts on the folding intermediates of SNAREs to chaperone their assembly.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the Munc18-1 activities observed.

claim: Baker et al. reported the crystal structures of fungus SM protein Vps33 bound with its cognate individual Vam3 and Nyv1 SNAREs.
source: During revision of this work, Baker et al. reported the crystal structures of fungus SM protein Vps33 bound with its cognate individual Vam3 and Nyv1 SNAREs (Baker et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on citation to recent structural work.

claim: Vps33 interacts with the entire Qa- and R-SNARE motifs through two non-overlapping surfaces on Vps33 and aligns the SNARE helical NTDs in proximity and register.
source: They found that Vps33 interacts with the entire Qa- and R-SNARE motifs through two non-overlapping surfaces on Vps33 and aligns the SNARE helical NTDs in proximity and register (state iii).
evidence: This is based on citation to the structural work.

claim: SM proteins serve as a template to initiate SNARE assembly into a partially zippered complex.
source: Because the structures of all SNARE complexes and SM proteins are highly conserved, they predicted that SM proteins serve as a template to initiate SNARE assembly into a partially zippered complex.
evidence: This is a prediction from the structural work cited.

claim: The discoveries of Munc18-1-mediated de novo SNARE assembly and half-zippered SNARE complex strongly support the prediction that SM proteins serve as a template.
source: Our discoveries of Munc18-1-mediated de novo SNARE assembly and half-zippered SNARE complex strongly support this prediction, which in turn offers a molecular mechanism for our observations (state iii).
evidence: This is a conclusion that the current work supports the prediction from structural studies.

claim: Representative SNARE complexes mediating diverse membrane trafficking pathways slowly initiate their NTD assembly and pause in half-zippered states.
source: In addition, we previously showed that representative SNARE complexes mediating diverse membrane trafficking pathways slowly initiate their NTD assembly and pause in half-zippered states.
evidence: This is based on previous work by the authors.

claim: These observations make SM-mediated SNARE assembly necessary.
source: These observations make SM-mediated SNARE assembly necessary.
evidence: This is an inference based on the slow intrinsic assembly.

claim: The N-peptide is essential for recruiting Munc18-1 to the fusion site to assist SNARE assembly.
source: Finally, the N-peptide is essential for recruiting Munc18-1 to the fusion site to assist SNARE assembly (Rathore et al., 2010).
evidence: This is based on citation to previous work.

claim: Once the trans-SNARE complexes are formed, the N-peptide is not required and can be cleaved from syntaxin SNARE motif without compromising the subsequent liposome fusion in vitro.
source: Interestingly, once the trans-SNARE complexes are formed, the N-peptide is not required and can be cleaved from syntaxin SNARE motif without compromising the subsequent liposome fusion in vitro, indicating that Munc18-1 binds the trans-SNARE complex in an NRD-independent manner before fusion (state vi).
evidence: This is based on citation to previous work.

claim: After trans-SNARE assembly, Munc18-1 switches to the NRD-independent Tc binding mode.
source: Consistent with this observation, we considered that after trans-SNARE assembly, Munc18-1 switches to the NRD-independent Tc binding mode observed by us.
evidence: This is an inference based on the current observations and previous work.

claim: Munc18-1 induces Tc folding and greatly stabilizes the t-SNARE to facilitate SNARE assembly and membrane fusion similar to Vc and Vn peptides.
source: Munc18-1 then induces Tc folding and greatly stabilizes the t-SNARE to facilitate SNARE assembly and membrane fusion similar to Vc and Vn peptides (Melia et al., 2002; Pobbati et al., 2006; Li et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on the current observations and citations to previous work on peptides.

claim: SM proteins act as chaperones to enhance SNARE assembly, which is essential for membrane fusion.
source: These comparisons suggest that SM proteins act as chaperones to enhance SNARE assembly, which is essential for membrane fusion.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on all the observations and comparisons with previous work.

claim: Munc18-1 and other SM proteins significantly enhance membrane fusion only under special conditions.
source: We noticed that Munc18-1 and other SM proteins significantly enhance membrane fusion only under special conditions.
evidence: This is an observation based on review of the literature.

claim: Incubating SNARE-anchored liposomes in the presence of Munc18-1 at 4ºC or adding crowding agents is required to observe Munc18-1-enhanced liposome fusion.
source: Shen and co-workers showed that incubating SNARE-anchored liposomes in the presence of Munc18-1 at 4ºC or adding crowding agents, such as 100 mg/ml Ficoll 70, in the fusion reaction is required to observe Munc18-1-enhanced liposome fusion (Shen et al., 2007; Yu et al., 2015).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous work.

claim: SM proteins appear to weakly associate with both Qa- and R-SNAREs to form the template that initiates SNARE assembly.
source: In general, SM proteins appear to weakly associate with both Qa- and R-SNAREs to form the template that initiates SNARE assembly (Parisotto et al., 2014; Xu et al., 2010b; Baker et al., 2015; Lobingier and Merz, 2012).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous work.

claim: The use of N-terminally crosslinked SNARE constructs may facilitate Munc18-1 binding to both syntaxin and VAMP2 to form the template required for SNARE assembly.
source: The use of N-terminally crosslinked SNARE constructs in our experiments may facilitate Munc18-1 binding to both syntaxin and VAMP2 to form the template required for SNARE assembly (state iii).
evidence: This is speculation about why the current experiments successfully observed Munc18-1 activities.

claim: The presence of a single SNAP-25 molecule in the experiments may increase the contrast to observe Munc18-1-mediated de novo SNARE assembly.
